content: 1. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration and pharmacological effect of pimavanserin by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. If co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the pimavanserin dose to 17 mg/day. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 2. Darunavir significantly increases the plasma concentration and effect of pimozide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of QT prolongation and other toxicities. Similarly, cobicistat also increases pimozide levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 inhibition, making this combination contraindicated. 3. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration of pioglitazone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 4. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration of pirtobrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib during the use of strong CYP3A inhibitors. Resume the original dose after discontinuing the strong inhibitor for 5 half-lives. 5. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration of pitavastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with cobicistat, start with the lowest recommended dose and titrate while monitoring for safety. 6. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration of pitolisant by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Reduce the pitolisant dose by half when initiating strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. Close monitoring is required. 7. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration of polatuzumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, and MMAE (a CYP3A4 substrate). Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase MMAE exposure, leading to enhanced toxicities. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration of pomalidomide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 9. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration of ponatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat also increases ponatinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. 10. Posaconazole increases the plasma concentration of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Posaconazole also increases cobicistat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, necessitating avoidance or alternative therapy. 11. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration of pralsetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat also increases pralsetinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. 12. Darunavir decreases the effects of pramlintide due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely for hyperglycemia. 13. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration of pravastatin by an unknown mechanism, likely involving CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Cobicistat also increases pravastatin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. 14. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration of praziquantel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration of prednisolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration of prednisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while prednisone decreases darunavir levels via the same pathway. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration of primaquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Primidone decreases the plasma concentration of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Primidone also decreases cobicistat levels via CYP3A4 induction, making this combination contraindicated as well. 19. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration of progesterone intravaginal gel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat also increases progesterone gel levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. 20. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration of micronized progesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat also increases micronized progesterone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. 21. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration of natural progesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat also increases natural progesterone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. 22. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration of propafenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Darunavir also increases propafenone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Clinical monitoring is recommended when co-administering with antiarrhythmics. 23. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration of protriptyline by an unknown mechanism. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible dose, and monitor closely during co-administration with cobicistat. 24. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration of quazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Darunavir also increases quazepam levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. 25. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration of quetiapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is necessary, reduce the quetiapine dose to one-sixth of the current dose and monitor for adverse reactions. 26. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration of quinidine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also increases quinidine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 27. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration of quinine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir also increases quinine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 28. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the plasma concentration of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration of quizartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the quizartinib dose and monitor closely. 30. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration of rabeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir also increases rabeprazole levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 31. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration of ramelteon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 32. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration of ranolazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Cobicistat also increases ranolazine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, making this combination contraindicated as well. 33. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration of red yeast rice by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Red yeast rice contains monacolin K, which is identical to lovastatin, and may increase the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. 34. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration of regorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase regorafenib levels while decreasing exposure to its active metabolites (M-2 and M-5). 35. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration of repaglinide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also increases repaglinide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration of repotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat also increases repotrectinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. 37. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration of resmetirom by an unknown mechanism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Resmetirom is an OATP1B1/3 substrate, and co-administration with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors should be avoided. 38. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration of ribociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A inhibitor is necessary, reduce the ribociclib starting dose to 400 mg/day. 39. Rifabutin decreases the plasma concentration of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the rifabutin dose to 150 mg orally every other day when co-administered with cobicistat. Monitor for rifabutin-associated neutropenia and uveitis. 40. Rifampin decreases the plasma concentration of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated.
